 The full lineup of nominations for the 2027 Grammys was announced Monday morning, and most of the top artists that had been predicted to score big came through with impressive tallies. But one piece of the puzzle definitely did not go as foreseen — that it would end up being Raye leading the pack, and just how big her haul would be.
 Raye leads all nominees with a startling 11 nods, followed by Rosalía with nine. Tied for seven nominations each are Ella Langley , Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers. Following close behind with six nods each are Bruno Mars , Leon Thomas and Olivia Dean .
 Related Stories 
 Taika Waititi Slams ‘Klara and the Sun’ Critics as ‘Irrelevant,’ ‘Sad Lost Souls’ and Says He Hasn’t ‘Read a Review’ in 15 Years: 'But I Do Listen to the People’ 
 It’s not necessarily a fresh angle to point out that the Grammys have been favoring female artists as of late, but the disparity in gender representation has never been as dramatic as it is this year. In the category of album of the year, which many consider the Grammys’ most prestigious award, the eight nominations boil down to seven women and just one man (Bruno Mars being the lucky exception in that bunch). The same seven-to-one split goes for song of the year. For record of the year, six of the eight nominations go to women artists, and even then, one of the other two is for a male group with a woman as the featured artist (Tame Impala featuring Jennie).
 Guys, step up.
 The album of the year category will see Raye’s “This Music May Contain Hope” and a deluxe edition of Rosalía’s “Lux” face off against Bridgers’ “Lost Weekend,” Dean’s “The Art of Loving,” Langley’s “Dandelion,” Mars’ “The Romantic,” Rodrigo’s “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” and Swift’s “The Life of a Showgirl.”
 With her nod for “The Life of a Showgirl,” Swift has tied the record for the artist to have the most consecutive albums nominated for record of the year: five. Only Kendrick Lamar joins her in having had that many new albums in a row compete for the big prize.
 This year, Swift claimed a total of five nominations, including entries in the top three categories — album, record and song of the year — plus pop duo/group performance and song written for a motion picture. She split her submissions for record and song, choosing “The Fate of Ophelia” for her entry in the former category and the Disney song “I Knew It, I Knew You” for the latter division, and that paid off with nominations for both. “I Knew It, I Knew You” is, of course, the song that’s up as a movie theme song, and the title track of “The Life of a Showgirl,” a duet with Sabrina Carpenter, made it into the duo/group division.
 Mars also took a similar approach to Swift in submitting different songs for record and song of the year, and it also paid off for him, as his album’s biggest hit, “I Just Might,” scored a chance at record, while arguably the most beloved track from his project, “Risk It All,” got the song of the year nom.
 Otherwise, most top artists submitted the same tune for record and song of the year, as reflected in the final nominations. The numbers nominated for both include Dean’s “Man I Need,” Langley’s record-breaking “Choosin’ Texas,” Raye’s “Where Is My Husband!,” Rodrigo’s “The Cure,” and Rosalía’s “Berghain.”
 Only two artists managed to score a nod in either record of the year or song of the year but not both. Tame Impala and Jennie’s “Dracula” is up for record but not song, and conversely, Ariana Grande’s “Hate That I Made You Love Me” made it in for song but not record.
 The eight nominees for best new artist include Langley, who has a rare shot at sweeping all four top general categories this year. The others are Angine de Poitrine, Geese, Slayyyter, Sienna Spiro, Don Toliver, Remi Wolf and the Womack Sisters.
 Hip-hop did not have a banner year as far as the Grammys are concerned, with Toliver’s best new artist nomination being the only representation for that genre in any of the top general categories.
 Others having a less stellar Grammy year than predicted include Harry Styles, who was completely shut out of the nominations. Noah Kahan also defied expectations by only picing up one nomination; although he had only been nominated for a Grammy twice before, he was predicted to have a bigger look this year with his blockbuster album and ticket sales and a degree of critical praise.
 The 69th annual Grammys will air Sunday, Feb. 7, 2027, at 4 p.m. PT/7 p.m. ET on ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu. The show will air live from Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.
